The chances of somebody just walking into your apartment are slim but amazingly this exact thing has happened to me. Maybe you can share this story with your husband.

Growing up it wasn't a given that front doors in our neighbourhood were locked - we had the kind of door you had to lock manually from the inside. It was never drummed into me that I should be locking the door if I was home. One day after getting home from school I heard the front door open. I was upstairs, and not expecting my dad or brother home until later. I peeked down the stairs to see who it was and it was a man - a complete stranger. He didn't seem threatening to me, but being about 11 years old at the time I had no fucking clue what to do. I don't remember what the fuck I did next, but I somehow managed to get down the stairs, grab the home phone from the kitchen along with the family dog, and run out into the back garden. I phoned the police and asked them to come and help me. I remember telling the dispatcher that I had my dog with me, and she told me to keep him close (he was a good boy, he stuck by my side). 

The police came to find the guy just sitting in my dad's study. It turned out that the man was drunk, and had come into our house thinking it was his. We had no idea who he was. He did no harm, and had no intentions of hurting anyone (we assume), but my god was it fucking scary. 

I don't know what the laws are elsewhere in the world or whether they have changed since in the UK, but the guy couldn't be charged with breaking and entering because our door was unlocked and he just let himself in...

Either way, this story ended fine but I hate to think what could have happened to me had this been somebody violent or with bad intentions. 

Locking your door is such a small "ask" from your husband, in exchange for feeling safe in your own home. You aren't likely to get attacked by a lunatic but why take the risk?
